verdict.call: Wait with positive bias -- not a full entry
verdict.note: Internal weighted estimate is 8.3% below consensus -- within reasonable range, no material contradiction.

key_finding.summary: Five executives (CEO McDermott, CFO Mastantuono, Vice Chair Tzitzon, Chief HR/AI Officer Canney, GC Elmer) simultaneously canceled scheduled 10b5-1 sale plans on 2026-02-06. 21 days later, McDermott bought 28,682 shares ($3.00M) in the open market at $104.60 -- his only open-market purchase since 2019, timed almost exactly at the SaaSpocalypse bottom.
key_finding.caveat: Small vs. his ~$8.77M in sales in Aug 2025 alone; insider ownership is only 0.14% company-wide; the cancellation wasn't total (Fipps didn't cancel), and 4 of 5 who canceled resumed routine selling within weeks.

sector_context.name: Enterprise software / AI agents
sector_context.narrative: "SaaSpocalypse": a new agentic-AI model (early 2026) sparked fear that AI agents make seat-based workflow software obsolete; IGV fell ~20%. Since Apr-May 2026 a reversal is emerging (IGV +40% in one month) as actual reports, including NOW's, show no disruption.
sector_context.relative_positioning: WDAY/CRM trade far cheaper on EV/Sales (3.15x/3.72x vs NOW's 6.91x) but grow much slower (~9-13% vs NOW's 22%). Sector is recovering but not yet richly re-rated.

elevator_pitch: NOW is the symbol of the SaaSpocalypse: -49% over 52 weeks on AI disruption fear, despite AI ACV actually accelerating past $1B (+40% qoq) and repeated beat-and-raise quarters.

The CEO put real money in at $105 in Feb 2026 and consensus (Strong Buy, $140 target) hasn't moved -- but two debt-funded mega-acquisitions (Moveworks + Armis) and a contracting margin are fresh, real risks.
Technical picture is still broken (below MA50/MA200) -- the recent jump needs confirmation, not chasing.
bull_case: 22% revenue growth is the fastest among enterprise software giants.
AI ACV crossed $1B, accelerating >40% QoQ -- direct quantitative rebuttal of the SaaSpocalypse thesis.
CEO backed words with a real open-market buy at the bottom, alongside a 5-executive sale-plan cancellation.
EV/Sales of 6.9x is a 5-year low vs. ~16x historical median, disconnected from fundamentals (Rule of 40 = 53.3).
Armis + Moveworks expand TAM into cybersecurity and AI agent orchestration, not just core ITSM.
Analyst consensus remains Strong Buy with target 44% above spot, despite the 49% drawdown.
bear_case: Net debt flipped from +$3.9B to -$3.8B within 1-2 quarters funding two mega-acquisitions -- real integration risk.
Non-GAAP operating margin fell 32.0% -> 29.5% QoQ as integration costs peak.
GAAP operating margin is only 11.4% vs 29-32% Non-GAAP -- the gap is stock-based comp, not cash.
Microsoft's near-free Copilot/Power Platform bundling inside M365 is the same disruption thesis that hasn't actually gone away.
Liquidity is at its weakest point in company history (current ratio 0.70) exactly as debt tripled.
Price is still below both MA50 ($104) and MA200 ($127) -- no confirmed trend reversal yet.
FY2023 net income was 2.3x operating income (likely one-time tax item), making the headline 57x P/E less reliable than it looks.
Insider ownership is just 0.14%; only the CEO actually bought, others resumed selling within weeks.
thesis_summary.decision_question: Will the growth premium re-rate, or is the AI disruption fear correct? Open question: is the recent +6% jump the start of a confirmed reversal, or another 'sell the news' setup like Q1 2026 (-17% despite a full beat)?

valuation.reverse_dcf_note: Regular DCF was abandoned (terminal value = 75% of EV, too sensitive to WACC). Reverse DCF: current price implies only ~14.3% 5yr FCF CAGR, well below the ~20-23% consensus actually forecasts -- a real fear premium, not just a rates effect.

positive: Continued AI ACV acceleration (field proof against SaaSpocalypse)
negative: 10Y yield keeps rising / Fed stays hawkish
Actual evidence of AI agents displacing seats in flagship accounts
Integration execution risk -- margin keeps deteriorating
Renewed large-scale insider selling with no offsetting buys

risk_management.thesis_changing_risk: A confirmed 2-consecutive-quarter slowdown in cRPO growth or AI ACV growth would confirm the SaaSpocalypse thesis rather than refute it, and reopen the downside multiple gap.

numeric_thresholds.break_below: 52-week low $81.24, on a closing basis, not intraday wick

dca_entries.trigger: Daily close above $104.09 (50MA) on above-average volume
Q3 2026 confirmation (~Oct 2026): cRPO >= 20% and AI ACV growth >= 30%

ground_rules: Exit on thesis break, not price

key_facts.balance_sheet: Net debt flipped from +$3.88B (FY25) to -$3.79B (TTM), funding the Moveworks ($2.85B) and Armis (~$7.8B) acquisitions; refinanced May 2026 via $4B fixed-rate senior notes (2028-2056).
key_facts.insider_activity: CEO McDermott's $3M open-market buy (Feb 2026) is his only one since 2019; insider ownership overall is just 0.14%.
key_facts.management: No CEO/CFO turnover in 6+ years -- rare stability for the sector.
key_facts.multiples: P/S at 6.8x vs. its own 5-year median of ~16x, despite still growing 22% -- the fastest of its peer set (WDAY, CRM).

checklist: cRPO (cc): confirm >=20% for 2 straight quarters, or break if <18%
AI ACV growth (quarterly): confirm >=30% streak, or break if <15%
Non-GAAP operating margin: confirm stabilizing >=29%, or break if <28%
Insider trading: watch for large-scale sale renewal without offsetting buys
